item.title: Who Am I
item.description:
Hongcong (Jasper) Chu: The unfaltering fool, the untamed madman, joyfully so.

As a candidate for a Bachelor of Economics, Hongcong (Jasper) Chu technically navigates a joint program between CUP and CUFE, but his academic heart firmly belongs to CUFE. He thrives in its inclusive environment, a stark contrast to the atmosphere at CUP, which he finds profoundly uninspiring.

While his high GPA paints the picture of a model student, this is a masterful illusion. Jasper is the furthest thing from a test-oriented student playing the system for grad school admission; he’s more likely to be found skipping class to immerse himself in a research project he genuinely loves. His course selection is a testament to this, guided purely by passion rather than the path of least resistance to an easy grade. When not staging his quiet academic rebellion, he’s an avid runner, cyclist, and heavy-load trekker. In meetings and presentations, he’s a notorious chatterbox with a mind that loves to wander down the most creative and delightfully random paths.

He is engaged in a variety of interesting studies, including:

  • Publish or Perish, Stay or Flee? The Great Reshuffling of China’s Innovation Landscape. (with Yiduo (Edwin) Wang) In Preparation

  • Disaster Bonds: The Lock-in of Innovators. In Prepartion

  • Greening the Cradle, Polluting the Neighbors: The Environmental Externalities of Political Hierarchy. In Prepartion

  • Transferred Social Responsibility: Government Disaster Bailout and Corporate Philanthropy. (with Chao Feng, Brian Lucey, and Miao Wang) Under Review at Journal of Development Economics

  • The Digital Unlock: How Big Data Bureaus Break Corporate Carbon Lock-in. (with Songhao Guo, Xinmin Zhang, Yiduo (Edwin) Wang, and Xiaoyin Yang) Submitted

  • Data-Driven Regulatory Revolution: How Big Data Management Bureaus Uncover Firm R&D Manipulation. (with Xiaoyin Yang, Chao Feng, Xinmin Zhang, and Hong Zang) Submitted

  • At the Eye of the Storm: How Anti-Corruption Reshapes Capital Allocation Efficiency. (with Chao Feng and Miao Wang) Submitted

Look, some of that research was the real deal—stuff I actually cared about. The rest? I was just a name on the author list to pay the bills. It all amounts to nothing anyway. Just be happy, and seriously, don’t grind too hard.
